## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: `refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored fingerprint of any already-tracked file it is given. If a tracked file has been hand-edited, the edit becomes the new trusted value, which undoes the tamper detection the PR description relies on. This review traced both new helpers against `verify` in `app/integrity.py` and read the added tests; it did not run them. `register_new_files` correctly skips names that are already tracked, and `test_register_preserves_existing_fingerprints` checks that with an edited tracked file.

## Changes
The PR adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`. Both read the JSON manifest, add fingerprints for the given names and write the manifest back. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which covers both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Stop refresh from overwriting tracked fingerprints — If you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was hand-edited, the edited file's hash replaces the original entry and `verify` then returns True. Line 17 assigns `entries[name] = fingerprint(root / name)` for every name, with no `if name not in entries` guard like the one in `register_new_files` at line 24. The PR body says "Existing fingerprints let verification detect hand-edited tracked files." The only refresh test, `tests/test_integrity.py:6`, passes an unchanged tracked file, so it cannot catch this. — Any refresh run that includes a tampered tracked file, such as a refresh over every file in the content root, records the tampered content as trusted, and the integrity check stops detecting the edit. — Fix: If refresh is meant only to add new files, keep existing entries as `register_new_files` does. If re-hashing tracked files is intended, say so in the PR description and docstring, and add a test where a tracked file is edited before refresh.
